headline: Room growth firms up, but cost investments squeeze profit
summary_short: Choice Hotels' Q2 2026 revenue rose 3.4% y/y to $440.8M as U.S. RevPAR gained 1.3% and global net rooms grew 2.6%, but net income fell 21.3% to $64.3M ($1.41 diluted EPS) on a wider reimbursable-cost deficit, SG&A timing, and higher D&A. Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% to $175.4M and adjusted diluted EPS rose 5% to $2.02.
summary_long: Q2 revenue rose 3.4% y/y to $440.8M on 6% growth in franchise/management fees, driven by higher international royalty fees and U.S. RevPAR/royalty-rate gains. GAAP net income fell 21.3% to $64.3M ($1.41 diluted EPS) on a higher reimbursable-property deficit tied to franchisee-tool investments, SG&A timing, and higher D&A from owned hotels and the Choice Hotels Canada acquisition, partly offset by higher franchise fees. Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% to $175.4M; adjusted diluted EPS rose 5% to $2.02. FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $635-650M on stronger RevPAR/rooms growth, while net income and diluted EPS guidance were lowered on higher reimbursable expenses, interest expense, and tax rate. Cash fell to $42.8M; liquidity totaled $475M, net debt/EBITDA 3.1x.

drivers.explanation: Franchise and management fees rose 6% to $188M on higher international royalty fees, franchisee programs/services revenue, and U.S. RevPAR/royalty-rate improvement; partnership services fees rose 6% to $29M on procurement services growth.

Operating income fell as a wider net reimbursable deficit tied to franchisee-tool investments, SG&A timing, and higher D&A on owned hotels and the Choice Hotels Canada acquisition outweighed higher franchise fees.
Margin compression is fully explained by operating income falling 16.4% while revenue rose 3.4%, i.e. costs grew faster than the top line.
Net income fell 21% y/y on the same reimbursable-deficit, SG&A-timing, and D&A drivers behind the operating-income decline, plus higher interest expense, partly offset by higher franchise fees.
Net margin fell as net income dropped 21.3% against 3.4% revenue growth, a mechanical effect of shrinking profit on a larger revenue base.
Basic EPS fell to $1.42 from $1.76 as the net-income decline outweighed roughly a 2.6% reduction in weighted-average diluted shares from continued buybacks.
Diluted EPS fell to $1.41 from $1.75 as the net-income decline outweighed the roughly 2.6% reduction in weighted-average diluted shares from continued buybacks.
Pretax income fell $22.7M: the $20.5M operating-income decline plus $2.3M higher net other expense, chiefly a $1.5M rise in interest expense and a $1.1M larger equity-in-net-loss of affiliates.
Cash fell to $42.8M as $67.4M of six-month operating cash flow and other inflows were outweighed by $107.5M of treasury-stock purchases and $26.3M of dividends paid.
Long-term debt rose as the Company funded buybacks, franchise-agreement acquisition costs, and hotel investments partly via $96.3M of net revolver borrowings drawn during the first half of 2026.
Equity rose to a $142.2M positive balance from a deficit a year earlier, continuing a rebuild as retained profitability outweighed ongoing share repurchases and dividends.
Weighted-average diluted shares fell 2.6% y/y to 45.4M as $107.5M of first-half share repurchases outpaced new issuance from option exercises.

Guidance was mixed: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA and RevPAR/rooms-growth ranges were raised on stronger operating trends, while net income, adjusted net income, and diluted EPS guidance were lowered on higher reimbursable expenses, interest expense, and a higher tax rate.

callSnippets.quote: Our second quarter results reflect encouraging progress across our key priorities, with U.S. net rooms growth improving for the second consecutive quarter to its strongest first-half performance since 2021 and U.S. RevPAR trends strengthening.
callSnippets.speaker: Dom Dragisich, Interim Chief Executive Officer

callSnippets.quote: Over the past several years, we've built a stronger commercial engine and technology platform, and we continue to invest in both.
callSnippets.speaker: Dom Dragisich, Interim Chief Executive Officer

callSnippets.quote: Our biggest opportunity now is sharpening execution—leveraging those capabilities to further enhance franchisee economics by increasing the number and quality of the guests we deliver while lowering operating costs.
callSnippets.speaker: Dom Dragisich, Interim Chief Executive Officer

callSnippets.quote: While we still have work to do, this business has significantly more potential, and I'm confident we can realize it.
callSnippets.speaker: Dom Dragisich, Interim Chief Executive Officer
